transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Since the divorce I eat huge meals by myself late at night because I’m embarrassed by how much I eat around other people. My sister noticed how I was acting and told me she was worried I was trying to "fill a hole" left by the split, which is what finally convinced me to come in today.

When these late-night eating episodes happen, do you feel like you lose control and eat an unusually large amount in a short time, or is it more that you’re eating more because of stress from the divorce?

It’s really a mix of both, because the loneliness from the divorce definitely triggered this, but once I start eating, it feels completely out of my control. It's like a switch flips and my hands just keep shoveling food in even while I'm telling myself to stop. I'll end up polishing off enough enchiladas and rice for a whole family in just one sitting.

How often have these out-of-control eating episodes been happening, and for how many months since the divorce? Also, do they continue even on days when you’re not feeling especially upset about the divorce?

This has been happening at least a few nights every week for close to a year now, ever since the divorce was finalized. It has become a set routine, so it happens even on days when I'm not feeling particularly upset. Just coming home to the quiet apartment in the evenings is enough to trigger the habit.
After these eating episodes, do you ever try to make up for them by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot? Or do you usually not do anything to compensate afterward?
No, I don't do any of those things to make up for the eating. Usually, I just feel incredibly miserable and bloated, and I end up just going to sleep.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent binge-eating episodes characterized by eating an unusually large amount of food with a clear loss of control, occurring a few nights per week for nearly a year, with marked distress/shame and no compensatory behaviors. This pattern is most consistent with binge-eating disorder, coded in ICD-10 under other eating disorders (F50.8). The divorce appears to be a psychosocial trigger but does not better account for the persistent syndrome.
